title: Design a Parking Lot
statement:
Design a parking lot with spots in three sizes: small, medium, and large. A car fits a spot of its own size or any larger size, so a small car can take any spot and a large car needs a large one. Write a `ParkingLot` class, built from how many spots of each size the lot has, with three operations:

- `park car size` parks the car `car`, whose size is `small`, `medium`, or `large`. It takes a free spot of the car's own size when there is one, and otherwise a spot of the next size up that has one free. It returns the size of the spot it took, or `full` when no free spot fits the car.
- `leave car` frees the car's spot and returns `true`, or returns `false` when the car isn't parked.
- `free size` returns how many spots of that size are free.

The first line holds three numbers: how many small, medium, and large spots the lot has (any of them can be 0). The second line is the count `q`. Each of the next `q` lines is one operation. Print the answer to every operation on its own line. Car names are single words, and a parked car doesn't park again until it leaves.

Input:

```text
1 1 1
8
park a small
park b small
park c medium
park d large
leave b
free medium
leave b
park d medium
```

Expected output:

```text
small
medium
large
full
true
1
false
medium
```

hints: You don't need an object for every spot. A count of free spots for each size is enough, as long as you also remember which size of spot each parked car took.
Put the three sizes in order from small to large. Then parking means starting at the car's own size and walking up until you find a size with a free spot.
When a car leaves, give back a spot of the size it took, which can be bigger than the car. A map from each car to its spot's size makes that one lookup.
